title: Climbing Stairs
statement:
You are climbing a staircase. It takes `n` steps to reach the top.

Each time you can either climb **1** or **2** steps. In how many **distinct ways** can you climb to the top?

This is the "Hello World" of dynamic programming. The recurrence `ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)` is the same as the Fibonacci sequence — can you see why?

editorial.approach: The number of ways to reach step `n` equals the number of ways to reach step `n-1` (then take 1 step) plus the number of ways to reach step `n-2` (then take 2 steps). This gives the recurrence `ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2)` with base cases `ways(1) = 1` and `ways(2) = 2`. Solve with bottom-up DP using two variables (O(1) space) instead of a full array: iterate from 3 to n, updating `prev1` and `prev2` at each step.
